terms.definition: The extension of an object is directly proportional to the force applied, up to the limit of proportionality.
terms.examiner: F = kx. Say "up to the limit of proportionality".

terms.definition: The greatest force or stress after which the material still returns to its original length when the force is removed.
terms.examiner: Beyond it the deformation is plastic.

terms.definition: Force per unit cross-sectional area, σ = F/A, in Pa.
terms.examiner: For a wire A = πd²/4: use the diameter, measured with a micrometer.

terms.definition: Extension divided by original length, ε = x/L; it has no unit.
Tensile stress divided by tensile strain, in the region where stress is proportional to strain.
terms.examiner: Gradient of the linear part of the stress–strain graph.

terms.definition: The maximum stress a material can withstand before it breaks.
terms.examiner: Read it from the highest point of the stress–strain graph.

terms.definition: A material that breaks with little or no plastic deformation, such as glass.
terms.examiner: Contrast with ductile (can be drawn into wires) and polymeric behaviour.
